top_repos.portability_reason: The filter families are header-only sample processors and the repository documents a real-time Cortex-M4 test, leaving only callback and parameter plumbing.
top_repos.value_reason: Header-only biquads cover all-pass, shelving, Linkwitz-Riley, Butterworth, band-stop, and constant-Q EQ forms already exercised on a Cortex-M4.
top_repos.port_idea: Lift the header-only coefficient and sample functions into a fixed Daisy/Teensy block, recalculate only on parameter changes, and flush denormals.
top_repos.note: Returning - Header-only biquads cover all-pass, shelving, Linkwitz-Riley, Butterworth, band-stop, and constant-Q EQ forms already exercised on a Cortex-M4.

top_repos.portability_reason: The runtime is a short dependency-free single header parameterized by sample rate; the FFT design utility is not required on the target.
top_repos.value_reason: The dependency-free 0BSD header turns parallel complex one-pole sections into an analytic signal, enabling compact frequency shifters and single-sideband effects.
top_repos.port_idea: Compile the float header directly in a 48 kHz callback, validate phase and amplitude against its design tool, then map the complex output into a quadrature modulator.
top_repos.note: Returning - The dependency-free 0BSD header turns parallel complex one-pole sections into an analytic signal, enabling compact frequency shifters and single-sideband effects.
top_repos.summary: IIR Hilbert filter: short, dependency-free, header-only C++

top_repos.port_idea: Run the genetic search on a computer, keep only the emitted Faust topology, then compile that fixed kernel for the MCU and bound every evolved delay.
top_repos.note: Returning - Crossroads evolves gain-and-delay effect topologies offline and emits Faust, making it a useful source of generated comb, FIR, soft-clip, and delay structures rather than a runtime dependency.
top_repos.summary: At the crossroads of programming your own audio effects, and letting your audio effects be programmed for you.

top_repos.portability_reason: The reusable header core is separate and process methods avoid allocation, but C++20 features, broad configuration, and optional plugin/convolution modules should be cut from the firmware build.
top_repos.value_reason: The MIT header library separates no-allocation fuzz, tube-preamp, tone-stack, fixed-buffer spring-reverb, and static oversampling blocks from optional plugin and convolution code.
top_repos.port_idea: Start with VintageFuzzDSP or one tube stage, disable oversampling, replace C++20-only conveniences if needed, then size spring delays explicitly before enabling reverb.
top_repos.note: New - The MIT header library separates no-allocation fuzz, tube-preamp, tone-stack, fixed-buffer spring-reverb, and static oversampling blocks from optional plugin and convolution code.

top_repos.portability_reason: The Faust kernels are extractable, but eight voices plus chorus, a 100,000-sample delay and four-comb reverb exceed a prudent internal-memory budget without reducing the configuration.
top_repos.value_reason: The Faust voice combines dual-oscillator hard sync, a Buchla-style wavefolder, filter-envelope poly-mod and vintage drift, while the effects file adds Juno-style chorus and tape-flutter delay.
top_repos.port_idea: Compile one mono voice first, keep hard sync plus wavefolder and filter, then shorten the 100,000-sample delay or move it to external memory before adding chorus, reverb, or polyphony.
top_repos.note: New - The Faust voice combines dual-oscillator hard sync, a Buchla-style wavefolder, filter-envelope poly-mod and vintage drift, while the effects file adds Juno-style chorus and tape-flutter delay.
top_repos.summary: A hardware-first web synth for your Arturia KeyStep and BeatStep. Minimal computer, maximal knobs, built for the jam flow state.
